extracted.intended_audience: authors, TPC members (reviewers), Track/Program Chairs participating in RTSS 2022 submissions and reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance for submitting and reviewing papers under the RTSS 2022 double-blind process, covering conflict-of-interest disclosure, anonymization, handling of de-blinding (e.g., arXiv/preprints/prior reviews), and roles of reviewers and Track Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author conflict-of-interest (CoI) disclosure responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must indicate any TPC members with whom they have CoIs as well as the types of CoIs. The submitter is responsible to collect the CoIs of every author of the submission and then enter them into the system before the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must enter all CoIs for every author prior to the submission deadline. This is the authors' responsibility; failure to do so would violate the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional CoIs notification and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may optionally indicate TPC members that they have a CoI with that is outside of the normal scope of CoIs (exceptional CoIs). This information, including proper reasons for the additional CoIs must be communicated directly to the Program Chair in writing prior to the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPC members listed as exceptional CoIs will not normally be eligible to review the authors’ paper(s). The final decision on whether to make this restriction rests with the Program Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: TPC member CoI declaration process
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the regular bidding phase, TPC members will be asked to declare CoIs based on a list of authors and affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list provided to TPC members will NOT include paper titles, abstracts, or paper IDs; CoI declarations should be made from author names and affiliations only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incrementality assessment independent of author identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Author identity does not determine whether a contribution is incremental; rather, the delta relative to the state of the art does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References are not blinded, and authors can (and must) discuss the state of the art objectively (including their own work in an anonymized form), so reviewers should assess incrementality based on the paper's relationship to the SOTA. Submissions that extend published workshop papers with DOI are handled differently—see double-blind submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to anonymize discussion of prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must discuss their own prior work in anonymized form while citing and discussing the state of the art objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because references are unblinded, authors should still present prior work in a way that preserves author anonymity (per the double-blind submission requirements) while giving reviewers enough information to assess novelty and incrementality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness judged only by the paper's content (no proof-by-authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Either a proof is clear and convincing, or it is not. 'Proof by authority' is not an acceptable scientific method, nor are prior mistakes sufficient justification for rejection of new results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate correctness based on clarity and rigor in the submitted paper. Empirical results should be judged on their merits, limitations, and weaknesses as presented, without regard to author or lab identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that double-blind is imperfect but still beneficial
rubrics_metrics.description: No double-blind peer-review process is perfect; papers may sometimes be de-blinded (e.g., distinctive authorship style, preprints, resubmissions). However, a double-blind process does not have to be perfect to be beneficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include enabling authors to craft less-attributable papers, changing reviewer attitudes to deemphasize author identity, and encouraging balanced presentation of prior work. Even plausible guesses about authorship should not give undue weight to identity in decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for arXiv (preprint) submissions under double-blind
rubrics_metrics.description: It is OK to submit a paper that is on arXiv to RTSS, but the submission should still follow the double-blind policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submission, the author must send a note and the arXiv version to the Program Chair to indicate the paper has been put on arXiv. Putting a paper on arXiv carries the risk of being identified but is not considered a violation if properly reported and anonymization rules are followed. Program Chair will instruct TPC members not to deliberately search for papers; if a member happens to see the paper on arXiv they should inform the Program Chair but must not reveal author identities to other TPC members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct regarding de-blinding and prior exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will not intentionally try to de-blind a paper (e.g., by searching the web). If TPC members feel they can de-blind a submission for any reason, they should not reveal their suspicion and should not let it influence their assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer can de-blind a submission based on title/abstract alone (e.g., they reviewed a prior version), they may still bid for the paper and should not declare a CoI solely for that reason because their expertise is required. If a reviewer has previously reviewed a prior version, they must not reveal that fact and must base their assessment exclusively on the present version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and exception for Track Chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The double-blind policy does not extend to Track Chairs (one of whom is the Program Chair), unless they have CoIs with the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track Chairs organize the peer-review process and therefore know all author identities, affiliations, reviewers, and assignments. If a Track Chair has a CoI with some authors, those papers will be handled by the other Track Chair or a senior, non-conflicted TPC member.
